preparer: Session D1 legal-design worker, executing rcap-va-2026-2027-statutory-cutover
decisionSource: Va. Code § 19.2-392.2 and § 19.2-392.6, each read in both published versions from the Virginia General Assembly's own publication at law.lis.virginia.gov, which serves the in-force and the future-effective text of a section on one page with its own historical citation. Read against the integrated Virginia legal-design memo, the normalized track registry, the packet-set manifests and the authoritative blocker ledger.
whatThisDocumentIs: The decision record that plans Virginia's two statutory cutovers. Six questions are answered separately: which version of § 19.2-392.2 governs a packet generated now, which takes effect on December 1, 2026, whether the change needs a successor track or a versioned packet or is carried by the existing tracks, what should happen to the four tracks' 2026-11-30 end date, whether current-law packets may be built and delivered before the cutover at all, and the exact copy and routing consequences. It also covers the § 19.2-392.6 change effective July 1, 2027 and the dated screening and regression requirements that follow. "Both versions exist" is not treated as an answer anywhere in it. It amends no memo, regenerates no registry, implements nothing and asserts no counsel approval.

scopeOfThisJob.trackTouched: None. This record adjudicates the cutover questions carried by five Virginia tracks and writes only itself.
scopeOfThisJob.questionsExpresslyNotReached: The form questions are untouched and remain open on their own owners: whether CC-1473 is revised for the December version, whether an official form exists for a subsection B identity-use petition or a subsection I pardon expungement, and the CC-1201 series retrieval failure the memo records. Whether automatic sealing has actually begun producing sealed records is a participant-instruction release blocker owned elsewhere. The seven Chapter 23.2 petition and automatic-sealing tracks are untouched except where § 19.2-392.6 reaches them.

methodNote: Both sections were read in both versions from the publisher that prints them side by side, and the two versions of § 19.2-392.2 were then diffed subsection by subsection rather than read for impression. That matters: the memo applies a single 2026-11-30 end date to all four § 19.2-392.2 tracks, and the diff shows the amendment does not reach all four. Six of the section's thirteen subsections are byte-identical across the two versions, which is what makes a per-track answer possible instead of a per-section one.

theDiff.method: The two published versions of § 19.2-392.2 were split into subsections A through M and compared word by word. Six subsections are identical; seven differ, and one of those seven differs only in a comma.

A.current: "If a person is charged with the commission of a crime, a civil offense, or any offense defined in Title 18.2, and 1. Is acquitted, or 2. A nolle prosequi is taken or the charge is otherwise dismissed, including dismissal by accord and satisfaction pursuant to § 19.2-151, he may file a petition …"
A.future: "If a person is arrested, charged, summonsed, or indicted for the commission of an infraction, a crime, or a civil offense and is not ultimately convicted, provided that no stipulation of facts sufficient to find guilt was entered or the court did not determine the facts sufficient to find guilt but deferred adjudication or disposition to a later date, such matter is eligible for expungement. Such person may file a petition …"
whatItDoes: Adds infractions to the covered offence classes.
Covers arrest, summons and indictment, not only being charged.
Replaces the closed list of qualifying dispositions — acquittal, nolle prosequi, otherwise dismissed — with a single test: not ultimately convicted.

Adds a carve-out that does not exist today: a matter is outside the section if a stipulation of facts sufficient to find guilt was entered, or if the court determined the facts sufficient to find guilt but deferred adjudication or disposition. That is a new screening question, not a relaxation.

changes: "the circuit court of the county or city in which the case was disposed of by acquittal or being otherwise dismissed" becomes "in which the case was resolved".
New sentence: "A single petition may request the expungement of the police and court records for multiple charges arising out of separate transactions or occurrences."
New sentence: "Such unavailability alone shall not be a basis for refusing expungement."

D.change: The attorney for the Commonwealth "may file an objection or answer to the petition, and if an objection is filed, shall include the basis for such objection".

F.kind: standard, scope of the order, and one express rule
changes: "manifest injustice" becomes "potential manifest injustice", in both places it appears.

The order may now expunge "any specifically identified emergency or preliminary protective orders issued pursuant to § 16.1-253, 16.1-253.1, 16.1-253.4, 19.2-152.8, or 19.2-152.9" along with the police and court records.
New sentence: "The existence of a prior conviction alone shall not be a sufficient basis to deny an expungement."

G.change: New sentence: "Any person whose petition for relief under this section is the subject of an appeal shall be allowed to proceed under a pseudonym pursuant to § 8.01-15.1 upon his request."

H.change: A serial comma after "indictment". No substantive change.

1_whichVersionGovernsAPacketGeneratedNow.answer: The version headed "(Effective until December 1, 2026)" — the text as it stands after 2025 cc. 634, 671. It governs today, 2026-08-08, and every day through 2026-11-30.
1_whichVersionGovernsAPacketGeneratedNow.whyThisIsAnAnswerAndNotAnObservation: A participant who files tomorrow files under it. The petition is a procedural instrument and the version in force when it is filed is the one the circuit court applies. Nothing about the December text is available to a petition filed before December 1, and a packet that offered it would be asserting law that is not yet law.
1_whichVersionGovernsAPacketGeneratedNow.operativeRule: Select by the date the petition is filed, not by the date of the offence, the date of the disposition, or the date the participant answered the intake. The section reaches conduct of any age; what moves on December 1 is the rule the court applies to the petition in front of it.

2_whichVersionTakesEffectDecember1_2026.answer: The version headed "(Effective December 1, 2026)", added by 2026 Va. Acts c. 1127.
2_whichVersionTakesEffectDecember1_2026.statusToday: future-effective law. It is not current law and must not be described, offered or screened against as if it were.

3_successorTrackOrVersionedPacket.answer: A versioned packet, keyed to the filing date, inside the existing tracks. No future-effective successor track, and no new node.
why: The amendment does not create a mechanism. It is the same section, the same petition, the same circuit court of the locality where the matter was resolved, the same absence of court fees, the same Commonwealth as party defendant, the same order forwarded to the Department of State Police under subsection K. What changes is who qualifies and how the petition may be packaged.

A successor track would put a second node in the registry for one route and would move Virginia's denominator for a change that adds no relief. Track identity is the relief route; the route is unchanged.
The registry models one effective interval per track, which is exactly why the cutover must not be expressed as an interval on the track. It is a content boundary inside the track.
And the change is not uniform across the four tracks, which a successor track could not express. Three of the four are keyed to subsections that do not move.

va_exp_nonconviction.affected: Yes, materially. All three of its governing subsections change, and A changes at the gateway.
va_exp_nonconviction.treatment: Two dated content versions behind one track, selected by filing date.

va_exp_identity_used_by_another.affected: Yes, but only procedurally. Subsection B, its own gateway, is byte-identical across the versions. What moves is C — charging document, "resolved", the multi-transaction single petition and the unavailability rule — and D's requirement that an objection state its basis.
va_exp_identity_used_by_another.treatment: Two dated content versions behind one track. Its eligibility copy does not change; its filing and objection copy does.

va_exp_absolute_pardon.affected: No. All three are byte-identical across the two versions.
va_exp_absolute_pardon.treatment: No versioning at all. This track is not part of the cutover and should never have carried a 2026-11-30 end date.

va_exp_actual_innocence.affected: No. Both subsections are byte-identical across the two versions.
va_exp_actual_innocence.treatment: No versioning. It is a process-guidance track and the guidance it gives is unchanged by c. 1127.

whatMustNotBeDone: Do not create a va_exp_nonconviction_2026 or any similarly dated sibling track.
Do not fold the four tracks into one because they share a section.
Do not version the two unaffected tracks for tidiness. A version boundary that changes nothing is a lie about the law and a fixture that will drift.

4_effectiveToTreatment.answer: Every one of the four tracks should carry effectiveTo null. None of them ends on 2026-11-30, and three of them are not touched by the amendment at all.
4_effectiveToTreatment.theProblemWithTheCurrentValue: All four tracks record effectiveTo 2026-11-30, which reads as the track expiring. It does not. Va. Code § 19.2-392.2 is in force before and after December 1, 2026, and the relief it gives — a petition to expunge police and court records — is available on both sides of the date. A registry that takes 2026-11-30 at face value would silently retire four live Virginia routes on 2026-12-01, which is precisely the failure the assignment forbids.
4_effectiveToTreatment.whatTheDateWasActuallyRecording: The end of the *content version* the memo was written against, which is a real and useful fact recorded in the wrong field. It belongs to the packet's version selector and to a track-level note, not to the track's effective interval.

required.va_exp_nonconviction: effectiveTo: null, with the 2026-12-01 content boundary recorded as a version note.
required.va_exp_identity_used_by_another: effectiveTo: null, with the same boundary recorded for its filing and objection copy only.
required.va_exp_absolute_pardon: effectiveTo: null, with no version boundary. Its subsections do not move.
required.va_exp_actual_innocence: effectiveTo: null, with no version boundary.

4_effectiveToTreatment.effectiveFromIsSeparate: The recorded effectiveFrom of 2025-07-01 is the date the current text took effect and is correct as such; it is not disturbed. On and after 2026-12-01 the date on which the operative text last changed becomes 2026-12-01, which is a currency statement for a later amendment to carry, not a reason to touch it now.

5_canCurrentLawPacketsBeBuiltAndDelivere.answer: Yes, and building only the December version would be the error.
why: The current version governs for the whole of the remaining window. Refusing to build it withholds relief that exists today from every participant who files before December 1.

Building the December version now and offering it would activate future law early, which the assignment forbids and which would put a petition in front of a circuit court asserting a gateway the court cannot apply.
The two are not alternatives. The build is dated: one content version in force now, a second that switches on at 2026-12-01, and a selector that reads the filing date.
5_canCurrentLawPacketsBeBuiltAndDelivere.whatStillHoldsDelivery: This answer removes the cutover as a reason not to build. It does not make any Virginia track deliverable. The four tracks are held by their own form questions — whether CC-1473 is revised for the December version, whether any official form exists for a subsection B identity-use petition or a subsection I pardon expungement, and the CC-1201 series that the memo records as unretrievable from the official library — and by counsel review. None of those is this record's to close and none of them is closed here.
5_canCurrentLawPacketsBeBuiltAndDelivere.sequencingConsequence: If the December content version is not ready by 2026-12-01, the correct behaviour is to stop generating on the affected tracks, not to ship the November text into December. A stale packet is worse than no packet: it would state a gateway the participant no longer has to satisfy and omit a broader one they now do.

mustState: The gateway as it is: charged with a crime, a civil offence, or an offence defined in Title 18.2, and either acquitted or the charge nolle prossed or otherwise dismissed, including dismissal by accord and satisfaction under § 19.2-151.
That the standard is manifest injustice, without the word potential.
That the petition is filed in the circuit court of the county or city where the case was disposed of by acquittal or dismissal.
That no court fees or costs are payable for a subsection A or subsection B petition.
That the Commonwealth's attorney has 21 days after service to object, answer, or give written notice of no objection.
mustNotState: That a single petition may cover charges from separate transactions or occurrences.
That a prior conviction alone cannot defeat the petition.
That the order can reach an emergency or preliminary protective order.
That an appellant may proceed under a pseudonym.
That an objection must state its basis.
The word potential before manifest injustice.
beforeTheCutover.routing: A participant with qualifying charges arising out of separate transactions needs one petition per transaction. The assembly emits N petitions, and the packet says why.

mustState: The gateway as it becomes: arrested, charged, summonsed or indicted for an infraction, a crime or a civil offence, and not ultimately convicted.

The new carve-out, in the participant's own terms: the matter is not eligible if a stipulation of facts sufficient to find guilt was entered, or the court found the facts sufficient to find guilt and deferred adjudication or disposition. This must be asked before generation, because a deferred-disposition participant who qualifies under neither version will otherwise be told they now do.
That a single petition may request expungement for multiple charges arising out of separate transactions or occurrences.
That the standard is potential manifest injustice.
That the existence of a prior conviction alone is not a sufficient basis to deny expungement.
That the order may reach specifically identified emergency or preliminary protective orders under §§ 16.1-253, 16.1-253.1, 16.1-253.4, 19.2-152.8 and 19.2-152.9, if the participant identifies them.
That an objection must state its basis, and that a person appealing may ask to proceed under a pseudonym under § 8.01-15.1.
That the petition is filed in the circuit court of the locality where the case was resolved, and that a missing charging document is not by itself a basis for refusing expungement.
onAndAfterTheCutover.routing: The cardinality inverts. One petition may now cover charges from separate transactions, so the assembly emits one document where it previously emitted several. That is a change in what is produced, not only in what is said, and it is the single largest downstream consequence of the cutover.

newScreeningQuestion.question: In that case, did you agree to a written statement that the facts were enough to find you guilty, or did the judge say the facts were enough to find you guilty and then put the decision off to a later date?
newScreeningQuestion.whyItIsNew: Today the gateway is the disposition type and this question is not asked. From December 1 the gateway is not ultimately convicted, with this as its express exception, so a matter that looks eligible on disposition alone may not be.
newScreeningQuestion.appliesFrom: 2026-12-01 only. Asking it before the cutover would screen participants out under a rule that is not yet law.

whatDoesNotChangeEither: The court: the circuit court of the locality.
The absence of court fees and costs on a subsection A or B petition.
The 21-day window for the Commonwealth's attorney.
The fingerprint requirement on a subsection B petition, and the fingerprint-card handling in subsection E, which is byte-identical.
Subsection K's forwarding of the order to the Department of State Police, and subsection L's three-year voidability of a non-compliant order. Both are byte-identical.

7_section19_2_392_6_effectiveJuly1_2027.whatChanges: One word, in subsection A only. The automatically sealed offence list changes "a misdemeanor violation of § 18.2-248.1" to "a misdemeanor violation of former § 18.2-248.1". Subsections B, C and D have a single version each and do not move.
7_section19_2_392_6_effectiveJuly1_2027.enactedBy: 2026 Va. Acts Sp. Sess. I, c. 1.
7_section19_2_392_6_effectiveJuly1_2027.whatItMeans: It is a conforming amendment tracking the fate of § 18.2-248.1 itself. The set of convictions eligible for automatic sealing is not enlarged or reduced by it; the same misdemeanour is described as a violation of a former section.
7_section19_2_392_6_effectiveJuly1_2027.designEffect: None on eligibility and none on what va_auto_seal_convictions tells a participant about which convictions seal automatically. What it does add is a third dated boundary in the Virginia set, and any dated fixture that quotes the offence list must know which side of 2027-07-01 it sits on.
7_section19_2_392_6_effectiveJuly1_2027.whatItDoesNotResolve: The memo's own finding that the § 19.2-392.6(A) automatic list is narrower than the § 19.2-392.12:1(A) petition list — it omits § 4.1-305 and subsection A of § 18.2-265.3 — is unaffected by this amendment and stays exactly as recorded. Nor does it touch when automatic sealing actually begins producing sealed records, which is a separate release blocker.

theGeneratorContract: Generation must take an explicit as-of date and must not read a clock implicitly. A fixture that renders differently depending on when the suite runs is not a regression test.
The as-of date is the intended filing date. Where a participant has not supplied one, the packet must not guess a future date to reach the broader gateway.
Version selection must be total: every date must resolve to exactly one content version, and an unresolvable date must fail closed rather than fall back to a default.

pinnedFixtureDates.expect: current § 19.2-392.2 content on all four tracks; no infraction, no multi-transaction, no potential, no pseudonym, no protective-order language; N petitions for N transactions.
identical to 2026-08-08. This is the last day of the current version and the boundary must be inclusive.

December content on va_exp_nonconviction and va_exp_identity_used_by_another; one petition may cover separate transactions; the facts-sufficient screen is asked; va_exp_absolute_pardon and va_exp_actual_innocence render byte-identically to their 2026-11-30 output.
va_auto_seal_convictions quotes the offence list without the word former.
va_auto_seal_convictions quotes the offence list with former before § 18.2-248.1, and is otherwise byte-identical.

negativeAssertions: No fixture dated before 2026-12-01 may contain the strings "infraction", "potential manifest injustice", "separate transactions or occurrences", "pseudonym", or a citation to § 8.01-15.1 in the § 19.2-392.2 packets.
No fixture dated on or after 2026-12-01 may contain the closed disposition list "acquitted", "nolle prosequi" or "accord and satisfaction pursuant to § 19.2-151" as the gateway.

The va_exp_absolute_pardon and va_exp_actual_innocence outputs must be byte-identical across the 2026-11-30 and 2026-12-01 fixtures. That assertion is what stops a later editor versioning tracks the amendment does not reach.
No fixture at any date may set a track's packet-readiness flag, enable a jurisdiction, or move a launch gate.
8_screeningAndDatedRegressionRequirement.whyDatedTestsAreTheDeliverable: A cutover is not a one-off edit. It is a rule the generator has to keep applying correctly on a date nobody will be watching. The fixtures above are the only thing that makes the November-into-December failure visible before a participant sees it.

terminalDispositionDetail.why: The narrowest accurate result, and it is a decision rather than a description. Each of the six questions has one answer; "both versions exist" appears nowhere as one.
